name: meeple-on-board-v1
description: ⚠️ 09/09/2026, THE COMMONS FLIP: THIS ARM NOW PINS THE PASSENGERS AS WELL. Dean ruled the commons in as the engine DEFAULT (docs/commons-handoff-2026-09-09-v1.md), which moved four leaves at once - rules.turn.visitCurrency to 'commons', rules.turn.bonusTiming to 'start', rules.turn.startingMeeplesPerColour to 0, and the Orchard door's printed draw to 2/2. An overlay that pins only what it is named for stops being the arm it is called, silently, which is the 05/09/2026 lesson written down: NAME THE PASSENGERS BEFORE RULING AN ARM IN. So the `set` below carries every leaf this arm's game relied on, whether or not it was in the original experiment. ⭐ 05/09/2026: DEAN RULED R17 IN AND THE ENGINE DEFAULTS MOVED WITH IT. The shipped game is now meepleAsCard true, meepleAsCardGoesTo 'board', slotToll 1 and meepleCapPerColour 2, which is exactly overlays/meeple-on-board-v1.overlay.json. ⚠️ SO THIS OVERLAY IS NOW A NO-OP: it names the same values the shipped defaults carry, and running it reproduces the base game exactly. Any delta it prints against the reference is sampling noise. It is KEPT rather than deleted because the reports that measured R17 name it in their filenames and their headers, and a named arm that has vanished is worse than one that does nothing. The game this arm was measured against is overlays/meeple-as-card-v1.overlay.json (the box destination, R17's own control) and overlays/meeple-loop-v1.overlay.json (the loop before R15). ⭐ R17, THE CLOSED RESOURCE LOOP (Dean, 05/09/2026). Handoff v2's arm let a meeple pay for a build, a Grow or a crate and then sent it to the BOX, and the measurement (docs/meeple-loop-measurement-2026-09-04-v2.md) found that is what killed the loop: meeples left the game 18.27 times a game against 9.44 visits, the median supply in the last third hit 0.0 and the hook collapsed 0.35 to 0.09. This arm changes one thing. A meeple spent as a card is now PLACED ON ANOTHER PLAYER'S NOTICE BOARD, in its own colour's slot, exactly as a visit places one, and the host takes it back on their Collect. It buys the payer NOTHING else: no door action, it is not a visit, and the bonus slot is untouched. The whole payment lands on ONE chosen host (Dean ruled a host per meeple on 05/09/2026 and then ruled it back to one per payment the same day, on the branching factor: per meeple measured at 25,827 ways to buy a single building at four seats against 4,063 here). Placing onto a slot that already holds a meeple costs one FLAT extra meeple of any colour, which goes to the box and is the only drain left bar the supply cap. Read the hook, the bonus mix four ways and the pool by round first, then the new line: how many meeples a game are PLACED as payment rather than spent as a visit, and who receives them. The control is overlays/meeple-as-card-v1.overlay.json, which is the same rules with the box as the destination. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved. ⚠️ 13/09/2026: rules.turn.selfVisitAllowed true and rules.economy.noticeBoardsBySeats.2 1 are pinned here because the shipped defaults flipped when the commons was deleted, so this arm stays the game it was.
